unit.sep: Construct mirror images and test geometric equivalence using explicit evidence.
unit.careers: Illustrative mathematical design,pattern checking and model communication;no professional or driving qualification.
unit.focus: Line/plane symmetry,plane reflection properties,Cartesian images,mirror equations,direct/opposite congruence,SSS/SAS/ASA-AAS/RHS and responsible uses.
unit.content: Symmetry; Reflection; Equations of Mirror Lines; Congruence
unit.phenomenon: A fictional stencil label confuses reflection with negative enlargement and calls equal angles alone a guarantee of equal size.
unit.supportingPhenomena: Ideal symmetry lines,actual plane-mirror predictions/observations,shifted mirror equations,labelled congruent copies and fully specified triangle cases.
unit.drivingQuestion: How do we use reflection in day-to-day life? Where do we use congruence in real life?
unit.storylineThread: Symmetry→plane mirror→fold/reflection properties→axis lines→diagonals→shifted equation→general slope→direct/opposite copies→SSS/SAS→ASA/AAS→RHS→use/advice→independent evidence.
unit.coreCompetencies:
Learning to Learn: the learner applies the properties of reflection to generate the image of an object on a given mirror line.
Creativity and Imagination: the learner locates the image of an object placed at a point in front of a mirror.
unit.values:
Responsibility: the learner takes care of the mirror used in reflecting corresponding images.
Respect: the learner recognises the input of every member of the team as they work in groups to make paper cutouts of different identical shapes to identify direct or opposite congruent shapes.
unit.pcis:
Road safety: the learner discusses with peers the applications of reflections and congruence on images formed by driving mirrors in enhancing road safety.
Environment and Technology: the learner selectively and cautiously collects and observes different objects from the immediate environment and identifies the lines and planes of symmetry.

sections.title: 1. Identify symmetry and explain a plane reflection
sections.prompt: Using CRG13,draw the two symmetry lines of the nonsquare rectangle and state how many the square has. For P(3,1)andmirrorx=0,give the reflected point and explain the equal perpendicular distances. In the physical plane-mirror interpretation,distinguish the virtual image behind the mirror from a real object. This written task is not an actual mirror-use observation.
sections.exemplar: The nonsquare rectangle has two midlines parallel to its sides;the square has four lines including both diagonals. P′(−3,1),each point3units perpendicularly fromx=0,with midpoint(0,1)on the line. An ideal physical plane mirror gives a virtual image behind its surface,not a physical object that can be touched there. Correct written reasoning does not certify unobserved mirror use.

sections.title: 2. Construct an image and determine a mirror equation
sections.prompt: Reflect the CRG13triangle in y=−x,plotting and labelling each image coordinate on equal-unit axes. Separately determine the mirror equation from U/U′andV/V′by midpoint/perpendicular-bisector construction;show both midpoint coordinates and check that the same line works for both pairs.
sections.exemplar: A′(−1,−1),B′(−1,−3),C′(−3,−2)by(x,y)→(−y,−x). Separate midpoints(−1,1)and(0,2)lie on y=x+2;both joining segments have slope−1andarebisected perpendicularly by the slope1line. Corresponding labels,equal unit scales and both pair checks are required.

sections.title: 3. Carry out triangle congruence tests
sections.prompt: For each CRG13caseS,T,W,H,N,state whether the supplied data guarantee congruence under the given correspondence. Name and justify the sufficient criterion,including the included-angle or right-angle/hypotenuse condition where relevant. Find W’s third angle and H’s remaining leg. Explain why the case with angles only cannot guarantee equal size.
sections.exemplar: S SSS;T SASwith50°betweenmatched4cmand6cmsides;W AAS/SAA,orASAafterderivingthirdangle70°;H RHSwithrightanglesC/F,equalhypotenuse5andmatchingleg3,remainingleg4. N AAAdoesnotfixsize,soitdoesnotguaranteecongruence. Every side/angle comparison must preserve the stated vertex correspondence.

sections.title: 4. Write checked advice with a model limit
sections.prompt: Write a short independent advice card intended for a classmate with one specific correct plane-reflection use and one congruent-copy/stencil use supported by a named valid test or checked geometry. State why the ideal equal-size plane-mirror model cannot automatically describe every driving mirror. Include a concrete benefit and a limit;no actual road visit,digital action,cutout handling or presentation is claimed by this written final.
sections.exemplar: Accept varied specific advice when the geometry is correct and checked:for example,equal perpendicular plane-image distances guide a labelled paper reflection,andmatchingall3–4–5sidescheckscongruenttrianglecopies bySSS. Many driving mirrors are curved and may alter apparent size/field of view,so a plane congruence model must not be transferred automatically. A valid message names the correspondence/model condition and useful benefit without claiming unobserved actions.
